thread:
nora_cs: Flagging an onboarding hiccup for Papertrailr. Their desktop quickstart intermittently gets 401/403 on /v1/embeddings. CI and server calls succeed.

nora_cs: They pasted this curl (token redacted):
```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX_TRUNC" \n  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

nora_cs: When it fails they get: `HTTP/2 401 {"error":"invalid_auth","message":"token missing or invalid for this route"}`. Request-ids: req_tnl1 and req_tnl2. Failures only from their dev machine and Electron test harness.

james_backend: any difference when they run from a plain terminal vs the electron app? ask for raw headers and exact token string length (redacted ok).

nora_cs: they sent a copied token string length: 48 chars but when they `echo "$TOKEN" | wc -c` on their machine it returned 49. they said the token was copied from an internal password manager and pasted into a .env file.

kevin_sdk: aha. sounds like a trailing newline or carriage return in the env var. Some clients (curl, node fetch) behave differently when header values include control chars: some proxies remove the header, others reject it. Ask them to run `printf "%s" "$TOKEN" | od -c` to inspect hidden chars.

nora_cs: customer ran `od -c` and saw a `\r` at the end of the token (carriage return). They said their password manager appended CRLF when copying on Windows.

james_backend: that explains intermittent behavior: some runtimes strip trailing whitespace, some send it verbatim. When the CR is sent, our auth layer fails signature parsing and treats token as invalid -> 401/403. Two quick fixes: trim the token when loading from env (server-side) and remove CRLF from stored secret in their vault.

kevin_sdk: for the SDK we should add an early sanity check on API key format and auto-trim whitespace/newlines, with a loud warning in logs if we modified the provided key. I'll propose a small patch to Node/Browser SDKs to trim and validate pattern (prefix sk_ + [A-Za-z0-9_-]{40,}). Filing ticket.

audit-bot: ticket created: eng-sdk/#4322 add-api-key-trim-and-validation -> backlog.

nora_cs: customer applied quick fix: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat token.txt | tr -d '\r\n')` and re-ran tests; all green. They updated their vault entry to remove trailing CR and re-ran onboarding.

james_backend: follow-ups: 1) KB snippet for CS: how to detect hidden chars (`od -c` / `xxd -p`) and recommended sanitize commands, 2) recommend password managers use "copy as plain text" on Windows or trim before storing, 3) include SDK warning + trim change in release notes.

kevin_sdk: I'll add the validation check and include a runtime warning like: "API key contained unexpected whitespace; value was trimmed for compatibility. Please rotate if you suspect corruption." Also note in SDK quickstart to check for trailing CRLF on Windows.

nora_cs: logging renewal-risk: low — customer paused ~24h but regained momentum after the fix. I'll schedule a short handoff call to review secret management best practices and attach the KB.

james_backend: quick KB commands to paste into ticket:
```
# detect hidden chars
printf "%s" "$TOKEN" | od -c
# strip CR/LF when writing env
printf "%s" "$TOKEN" | tr -d '\r\n' > .env
```

kevin_sdk: thanks. will include a tiny unit test in SDK that fails when key contains non-printable chars.

nora_cs: closing loop with Papertrailr, adding transcript and the KB snippet to the support ticket. :white_check_mark:
